links.outcome: FairOdds-AUC and equalized odds after bias mitigation versus unmitigated baseline, with AUROC effect
links.effect: IPW and AFC significantly improved FairOdds-AUC over baseline (p<1e-12) across backbones and sites, e.g., IPW transformer 0.562 to 0.600 with essentially same discrimination; ColRm and ThreshOpt performed similar to baseline.
links.quote: FairOdds-AUC heatmaps show that IPW (0.574 [0.556, 0.593] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.600 [0.575, 0.629]) and AFC (0.573 [0.559, 0.588] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.613 [0.595, 0.629]) were bias mitigation techniques that consistently performed significantly better than the baseline approach without bias mitigation (0.547 [0.512, 0.570] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.562 [0.544, 0.578]) across modeling architecture backbones and evaluation sets, striking a balance between AUC performance and fairness (p < 1e-12 [IPW, baseline], p < 1e-12 [AFC, baseline]).

links.outcome: Subgroup fairness gaps (equalized odds by sex and race/ethnicity) across internal and external sites
links.effect: Baseline and column remover had sex EO >0.298; a trade-off was seen between AUROC and equalized odds gaps across sites, with no method excelling on both.
links.quote: For sex EO, baseline and column remover performed poorly (EO > 0.298 [0.276, 0.322]), while adversarial classifier (EO < 0.220 [0.191, 0.257]) and, to some extent, threshold optimization performed better across test sets (EO < 0.243 [0.213, 0.299]).

links.outcome: Fairness and performance generalization of mitigation methods across two external sites
links.effect: Inprocessing methods (IPW, AFC) generalized consistently across internal and two external sites; pre/postprocessing methods showed weaker generalizability and dataset-dependent effects.
links.quote: Postprocessing and preprocessing bias mitigation strategies yielded more variable FairOdds-AUC changes (-0.009 to +0.021) and showed weaker generalizability across external sites.

links.outcome: Whether combined performance-fairness metric changes choice of best model versus accuracy alone
links.effect: FairOdds-AUC with tunable lambda changed which mitigation strategy appeared optimal (ColRm/IPW at λ=0.1, IPW/AFC at λ=1, AFC at λ=10); demonstrates accuracy-only comparison would miss fairness differences.
links.quote: The choice of λ alters which mitigation strategy appears optimal.

links.effect: IPW improved FairOdds-AUC from 0.562 (95% CI 0.540, 0.581) to 0.600 (0.575, 0.629) for transformer and 0.556 (0.534, 0.577) to 0.5922 (0.53, 0.61919) for FCN, while maintaining discrimination; AFC reached up to 0.613 (0.595, 0.629).
